transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because after my cashier shifts, I keep buying huge takeout orders—burgers, fries, chicken, desserts, enough for a family—and then I’ll eat almost all of it myself before I even go home.
After you eat all that food, do you ever try to get rid of it or make up for it—like making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting afterward, or exercising a lot?
I’m not sure what you mean by making up for it. I know I eat a lot after work, but I haven’t really thought about it that way.
During these episodes after work, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating, even if you want to?
Yeah. Once I take that first bite, it’s like something clicks off. Even when I’m telling myself, “Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,” I just keep reaching for the next thing.
How many days per week, on average, do these after-work eating episodes happen?
For the last several months, it’s been three or four nights most weeks. Since the foreclosure calls started, I can’t remember a week where it didn’t happen at least once.
During these episodes, do you notice things like eating much faster than usual, eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or eating alone because you feel embarrassed about how much you're eating?
Yeah. A lot of nights I keep eating until my stomach is tight and hurting so bad I have to lean the seat back in the car, or lie still in bed and wait for it to pass.
How do you feel emotionally after these eating episodes—do you experience feelings like guilt, disgust with yourself, or significant distress about what happened?
I’m not really sure how to put it. Afterward I mostly just feel kind of bad and sit with it for a while.
Would you say your view of yourself—how good or bad you feel about who you are—is strongly tied to your weight or body shape?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about my weight or body shape being tied to how I see myself.
Would you say the way you eat during these episodes causes you real distress or upset, separate from just feeling physically uncomfortable afterward?
I’m not sure. I know I feel bad afterward, but I don’t really know if it’s the eating itself or just how physically awful I feel once I’ve done it.
Setting aside how your stomach feels physically, do you ever feel upset, ashamed, or guilty with yourself specifically about the fact that you ate that much or lost control?
I don't know. I mean, I feel bad afterward, but I haven't really separated whether I'm upset with myself about eating that much or just feeling sick and uncomfortable.

When you think about these episodes afterward, do you ever feel worried, frustrated, or upset with yourself about the fact that you couldn't control your eating—separate from how your body feels physically?

Yeah. Once I take that first bite, it’s like something clicks off. Even when I’m telling myself, “Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,” I just keep reaching for the next thing. That part really gets to me afterward.
